claim: Zebrafish are widely studied and relatively easy to culture using commercial systems.
source: Zebrafish are widely studied and relatively easy to culture using commercial systems.
evidence: This is a general statement about zebrafish in the abstract, drawing from established scientific knowledge about zebrafish as model organisms.

claim: A challenging aspect of maintaining aquatic facilities is animal feeding, which is both time- and resource-consuming.
source: However, a challenging aspect of maintaining aquatic facilities is animal feeding, which is both time- and resource-consuming.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about the challenges of aquatic facility maintenance.

claim: ZAF is reliable, provides a standardized amount of food to every tank, is cost-efficient and easy to build.
source: ZAF is reliable, provides a standardized amount of food to every tank, is cost-efficient and easy to build.
evidence: This is a direct assertion by the authors about the properties of their device, supported by the design and testing described in the manuscript.

claim: ZAF+ allows for the precise control of food distribution as a function of fish density per tank.
source: The advanced version, ZAF+, allows for the precise control of food distribution as a function of fish density per tank, and has a user-friendly interface.
evidence: This claim is supported by the design features described in the manuscript and demonstrated in the experiments.

claim: Both ZAF and ZAF+ are adaptable to any laboratory environment and facilitate the implementation of aquatic colonies.
source: Both ZAF and ZAF+ are adaptable to any laboratory environment and facilitate the implementation of aquatic colonies.
evidence: This is an assertion by the authors based on the modular design of the systems.

claim: The design is modular and can be scaled to meet different user needs.
source: Importantly, the design is modular and can be scaled to meet different user needs.
evidence: This is supported by the description of the system architecture and the authors' design choices.

claim: ZAF and ZAF+ do not adversely affect zebrafish culture.
source: Furthermore, our results show that ZAF and ZAF+ do not adversely affect zebrafish culture, enabling fully automatic feeding for any aquatic facility.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on fish weight, mortality, and spawning success.

claim: Zebrafish are vertebrates and have excellent optical properties as well as accessible genetics.
source: Among their advantages, zebrafish are vertebrates and have excellent optical properties as well as accessible genetics.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about zebrafish as a model organism.

claim: Zebrafish have low maintenance and husbandry cost.
source: Another essential feature of zebrafish is their low maintenance and husbandry cost (Westerfield, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Westerfield, 2000.

claim: The development of commercial systems for zebrafish culture has helped advance zebrafish research.
source: The development of commercial systems for zebrafish culture has helped advance zebrafish research (Lawrence, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lawrence, 2007.

claim: Implementing a zebrafish facility remains a challenge for many small to medium sized laboratories due to cost and infrastructure issues.
source: However, implementing a zebrafish facility remains a challenge for many small to medium sized laboratories due to cost and infrastructure issues.
evidence: This is an assertion based on general knowledge of laboratory constraints.

claim: The most important aspect of zebrafish husbandry is the feeding, usually done manually at least two times a day by dedicated staff.
source: The most important aspect of zebrafish husbandry is the feeding, usually done manually at least two times a day by dedicated staff, using dry or living food like Artemia nauplii (Lawrence, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lawrence, 2011, and reflects standard practice in zebrafish husbandry.

claim: Manual feeding is not sufficiently accurate and can be time and resource prohibitive for labs without dedicated staff.
source: Overall, manual feeding is not sufficiently accurate and can be time and resource prohibitive for labs without dedicated staff (Candelier et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Candelier et al., 2019.

claim: Very few technologies have been developed to automate zebrafish feeding and husbandry.
source: Very few technologies have been developed to automate zebrafish feeding and husbandry to help offset the challenges associated with implementing an aquatic facility.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the authors' review of existing technologies.

claim: Some vendors propose fully automated solutions, but these are typically expensive, proprietary, incompatible with other systems, and require manual food filling before each feeding session.
source: Some vendors propose fully automated solutions, but these are typically expensive, proprietary, incompatible with other systems, and require manual food filling before each feeding session.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the authors' knowledge of commercial products.

claim: Other groups have recently published semi-automatic solutions that require human supervision.
source: Other groups have recently published semi-automatic solutions that require human supervision (Candelier et al., 2019; Tangara et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Candelier et al., 2019 and Tangara et al., 2019.

claim: There is no open access and fully automated solution currently available.
source: However, there is no open access and fully automated solution currently available.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the authors' review of existing technologies.

claim: ZAF is optimised for simplicity to facilitate adoption, avoiding complex 3D printing, mechanical assembly, or complex circuit board manufacturing.
source: Importantly, such a design should be optimised for simplicity to facilitate adoption, avoiding complex 3D printing, mechanical assembly, or complex circuit board manufacturing.
evidence: This is supported by the design choices described in the manuscript.

claim: ZAF is easily assembled from inexpensive and commercially available parts.
source: It should be easily assembled from inexpensive and commercially available parts, making it maximally accessible for non-experts.
evidence: This is supported by the parts list and construction instructions provided.

claim: ZAF can be used for automatic feeding of zebrafish as well as for any similar aquatic model organism.
source: Here, we present ZAF (Zebrafish Automated Feeding) which satisfies all these requirements for automatic feeding of zebrafish as well as for any similar aquatic model organism.
evidence: This is an assertion by the authors based on the design of the system.

claim: The colony requires a dedicated room with specific characteristics (e.g. temperature, water source, drain access, etc.) and regular monitoring by committed staff.
source: The colony requires a dedicated room with specific characteristics (e.g. temperature, water source, drain access, etc.) and regular monitoring by committed staff.
evidence: This reflects standard requirements for zebrafish facilities based on established knowledge.

claim: The facility was enclosed inside of a large indoor tent and equipped with a smart heating system to control the temperature, a carbon purifier to regulate humidity and odors, cameras for remote monitoring, and water sensor ropes to detect leaks.
source: We then enclosed this system inside of a large indoor tent (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), and equipped this tent with a smart heating system to control the temperature, a carbon purifier to regulate humidity and odors, cameras for remote monitoring, and water sensor ropes to detect leaks.
evidence: This is a description of the authors' facility setup, supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ZAFs are affordable and leveraging only commercially available parts.
source: ZAFs are affordable and leveraging only commercially available parts (Supplementary files 2 and 3)
evidence: This is supported by the parts lists provided in the supplementary files.

claim: ZAF's design relies on mixing water with dry zebrafish food and then distributing this mix to all fish tanks.
source: ZAF's design relies on mixing water with dry zebrafish food and then distributing this mix to all fish tanks.
evidence: This is a description of the basic operating principle of ZAF.

claim: A servo motor rotates a food canister to dispense food into a container directly filled with water.
source: The basic operating principle of ZAF is simple: a servo motor rotates a food canister to dispense food into a container directly filled with water.
evidence: This is a description of the mechanism, supported by the design schematics.

claim: ZAF consists of three main modules: (i) electronics, (ii) tubing and pumps, and (iii) food preparation.
source: ZAF consists of three main modules: (i) electronics, (ii) tubing and pumps, and (iii) food preparation (Figure 1a and b).
evidence: This is supported by the description and Figure 1a and b.

claim: The electronics module is comprised of a credit card-sized computer (Raspberry Pi 3 B+) augmented with an extension board ('servo hat') that sends signals to various motor controllers.
source: The electronics module is comprised of a credit card-sized computer (Raspberry Pi 3 B+) augmented with an extension board ('servo hat') that sends signals to various motor controllers to trigger pumping and valve opening (detailed description of the electronic circuit in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and more construction details in the Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by the description and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Raspberry Pi 3 B + is connected to a touch screen and keyboard for easy user interfacing with the command-line interface.
source: The Raspberry Pi 3 B + is connected to a touch screen and keyboard for easy user interfacing with the command-line interface.
evidence: This is a description of the user interface setup.

claim: The amount of food delivered is constant across all tanks and can be modified by adjusting the food container opening as well as the degree of servo rotation.
source: The amount of food delivered is constant across all tanks and can be modified by adjusting the food container opening as well as the degree of servo rotation.
evidence: This describes the calibration mechanism of ZAF.

claim: In ZAF, an air pump is used to stir and mix the food and water.
source: In ZAF, an air pump is used to stir and mix the food and water (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by the description and Figure 1a.

claim: Building ZAF in a few hours is feasible by following the instructions on the publicly available wiki.
source: Once all parts have been delivered (see detailed list on Supplementary file 2), building ZAF in a few hours is feasible by following the instructions on our publicly available wiki.
evidence: This is an assertion by the authors based on their experience building the system.

claim: Both ZAF systems are highly modular and scalable: the number of tanks can be easily increased to meet the needs of larger aquatic facilities.
source: Both ZAF systems are highly modular and scalable: the number of tanks can be easily increased to meet the needs of larger aquatic facilities.
evidence: This is supported by the modular design described in the manuscript.

claim: There was no statistical difference in mean weight of adult fish fed with ZAF versus manual feeding over 8 weeks.
source: For this, we measured the weight of adult fish fed with the two techniques over 8 weeks and found no statistical difference (Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: There was no excess mortality over the 8-week period for fish fed with the automatic device (zero fish died out of 92) versus manual feeding (one fish died out of 33).
source: Additionally, we found no excess mortality over the 8-week period for fish fed with the automatic device (zero fish died out of 92) versus manual feeding (one fish died out of 33).
evidence: This claim is supported by mortality data collected during the experiment.

claim: There was no difference in fecundity between fish fed with ZAF and those fed manually.
source: During the same period, we evaluated the fecundity of the fish and observed no difference between the two populations (Figure 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by spawning success data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The automatic feeding does not affect the water quality of the facility over a period of three months.
source: Additionally, the automatic feeding does not affect the water quality of our facility over a period of three months (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by water quality data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: ZAF is appropriate for the feeding of a homogeneous fish population (i.e. tanks with a relatively equivalent number of animals).
source: Taken together, ZAF is appropriate for the feeding of a homogeneous fish population (i.e. tanks with a relatively equivalent number of animals) and it does not affect fish health nor fecundity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the design limitations of ZAF and the experimental results.

claim: ZAF lacks precise control of food distribution to individual tanks.
source: While ZAF is an effective system for feeding multiple tanks with similar numbers of animals, it lacks precise control of food distribution to individual tanks.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors based on the design of ZAF.

claim: ZAF+ was created to control food flow both spatially and temporally by adding valves upstream of each tank.
source: To overcome this problem, ZAF+ was created to control food flow both spatially and temporally by adding valves upstream of each tank (Figure 2a and b).
evidence: This is supported by the description and Figure 2a and b.

claim: The ZAF+ software allows users to configure feeding parameters such as feeding frequency, timing, and quantity, as well as which tanks need feeding.
source: The ZAF+ software allows users to configure feeding parameters such as feeding frequency, timing, and quantity, as well as which tanks need feeding.
evidence: This is a description of the software capabilities of ZAF+.

claim: ZAF+ allows users to individually control and distribute a precise amount of food for each tank.
source: With this system users can individually control and distribute a precise amount of food for each tank.
evidence: This is supported by the design features of ZAF+.

claim: ZAF+ was built by reusing several ZAF modules.
source: ZAF+ was built by reusing several ZAF modules.
evidence: This describes the relationship between ZAF and ZAF+ designs.

claim: ZAF+ is larger (21" w x 12" d x 9" h) than the base ZAF version but still fits in a fish facility.
source: ZAF+ is larger (21" w x 12" d x 9" h) than the base ZAF version but still fits in a fish facility.
evidence: This provides dimensional specifications of ZAF+.

claim: A micro-controller (Arduino Mega) was added to control the additional valves in ZAF+.
source: To control the additional valves we added a micro-controller (Arduino Mega) for all pumps and valves, which permits limitless scalability by daisy-chaining multiple such controllers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the description and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: ZAF+ can operate 7 days a week all year long, only requiring regular dry-food reloading as well as tube replacement.
source: ZAF+ can operate 7 days a week all year long, only requiring regular dry-food reloading as well as tube replacement.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the authors' experience operating ZAF+.

claim: Replacing tubing every 12 weeks takes one hour and is sufficient to keep tubes reasonably clean.
source: In our hands, we found that replacing tubing every 12 weeks takes one hour and is sufficient to keep tubes reasonably clean (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: There was no difference in the mean weights of fish fed with ZAF+ compared to the manually fed control group over 8 weeks.
source: The fish were assessed for mean weight over 8 weeks. Overall, we observed no difference in the mean weights compared to the manually fed control group (Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: There were no significant differences in reproduction between fish fed with ZAF+ and fish fed manually.
source: We then evaluated the reproduction of fish fed with ZAF+ and found no significant differences with fish fed manually.
evidence: This claim is supported by spawning success data.

claim: ZAF+ does not affect the water quality during a three months period.
source: Finally, ZAF+ does not affect the water quality during a three months period (Figure 1—figure supplement 4) nor fish mortality.
evidence: This claim is supported by water quality data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: ZAF+ is a viable solution for full feeding automation in aquatic facilities.
source: Thus, ZAF+ is a viable solution for full feeding automation in aquatic facilities.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results showing no adverse effects on fish health, reproduction, or water quality.

claim: ZAFs can help disseminate aquatic animal models in research institutes.
source: ZAFs are effective and cheap solutions to overcome staffing issues on weekends and holidays and we hope will help disseminating aquatic animal models in research institutes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential impact of ZAFs.

claim: ZAF devices can be easily adapted to behavioral studies (i.e. food conditioning) as well as any type of experimental design that requires pellets or liquid delivery.
source: Interestingly, our devices can be easily adapted to behavioral studies (i.e. food conditioning) as well as any type of experimental design that requires pellets or liquid delivery, illustrating the versatility of our system.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications of the system.

claim: Both ZAF designs are fully open access (hardware and software), modular, scalable and highly adaptable.
source: Both designs are fully open access (hardware and software), modular, scalable and highly adaptable.
evidence: This is supported by the availability of all blueprints, parts lists, and software on the public repository.

claim: ZAFs can easily be adapted to all commercially available aquatic facilities.
source: Importantly, ZAFs can easily be adapted to all commercially available aquatic facilities.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the modular design of the systems.

claim: ZAF+ is more robust than ZAF due to conceptual and technical improvements.
source: ZAF+ is more robust than ZAF due to conceptual and technical improvements.
evidence: This is an assertion by the authors based on the design improvements in ZAF+.

claim: ZAF is easy to build but does not offer control over food distribution per tank.
source: While ZAF is easy to build, it does not offer control over food distribution per tank.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors based on the design of ZAF.

claim: ZAF+ construction is more complex but is amenable to feeding variable numbers of fish per tank, or different tank sizes.
source: ZAF+ construction is more complex but is amenable to feeding variable numbers of fish per tank, or different tank sizes (Box 2).
evidence: This is supported by the design features of ZAF+ described in the manuscript.

claim: Both ZAF devices can run 7 days a week all year long.
source: Both devices can run 7 days a week all year long.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the authors' experience operating the devices.

claim: Manual cleaning or replacing of the tubes every 10 weeks is recommended for optimal performance.
source: For optimal performance, we do recommend manual cleaning or replacing of the tubes every 10 weeks.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the authors' experience.

claim: The authors tested both ZAF systems in their fish facility for a total of 19 months (9 months for ZAF and 10 months for ZAF+) and never suffered from major malfunctions.
source: We tested both ZAF systems in our fish facility for a total of 19 months (9 months for ZAF and 10 months for ZAF+) and never suffered from major malfunctions, nor observed adverse health effects to our fish.
evidence: This is based on the authors' long-term testing experience.

claim: The authors never observed adverse health effects to their fish during 19 months of testing ZAF systems.
source: We tested both ZAF systems in our fish facility for a total of 19 months (9 months for ZAF and 10 months for ZAF+) and never suffered from major malfunctions, nor observed adverse health effects to our fish.
evidence: This is based on the authors' long-term testing experience.

claim: Lab automation is likely to be increasingly critical to improve productivity, efficiency and research reproducibility.
source: Lab automation is likely to be increasingly critical to improve productivity, efficiency and research reproducibility (Check Hayden, 2014; Boyd, 2002; Almada et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Check Hayden, 2014; Boyd, 2002; and Almada et al., 2019.

claim: The field of animal husbandry has not yet made enough progress toward full automation.
source: However, the field of animal husbandry has not yet made enough progress toward full automation and this holds particularly true for aquatic facilities, which have not been modernized for decades.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the authors' assessment of the field.

claim: Aquatic facilities have not been modernized for decades.
source: However, the field of animal husbandry has not yet made enough progress toward full automation and this holds particularly true for aquatic facilities, which have not been modernized for decades.
evidence: This is an assertion based on the authors' assessment of the field.

claim: The authors used inexpensive hardware such as the micro-computer Raspberry-Pi, the Arduino micro-controller, and the Python programming language.
source: We used inexpensive hardware such as the micro-computer Raspberry-Pi (Gay, 2014), the Arduino micro-controller, and the Python programming language (Van Van Rossum, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by the description of the hardware components and citations.

claim: Dry food (Gemma from Skretting Zebrafish) has a complete nutritional profile and positive effect on fish health.
source: In this work we have used dry food (Gemma from Skretting Zebrafish) because of its complete nutritional profile and positive effect on fish health (Lawrence, 2011; Lawrence et al., 2012; Barton et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lawrence, 2011; Lawrence et al., 2012; and Barton et al., 2016.

claim: Automated feeding is most easily performed with dry food.
source: Automated feeding is most easily performed with dry food; however, the food container can be adapted to live food if required (data not shown).
evidence: This is an assertion based on practical considerations of the feeding system.

claim: The authors tested ZAF and ZAF+ with Artemia nauplii and the feeding works well.
source: We tested ZAF and ZAF+ with Artemia nauplii and the feeding works well.
evidence: This is based on the authors' testing experience.

claim: The automatic feeders can be easily adapted to deliver different types of food specific to different ages by adding several servos and food containers.
source: While we did not directly test breeding, our automatic feeders can be easily adapted to deliver different types of food specific to different ages by adding several servos and food containers.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential adaptations of the system.

claim: Both ZAF systems could be adapted to other aquatic species with similar breeding requirements as zebrafish.
source: With the advent of new aquatic model organisms with similar breeding requirements as zebrafish (Lawrence, 2011; Lawrence et al., 2012; Barton et al., 2016), it is conceivable that both ZAF systems could be adapted to others species.
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations about aquatic model organisms.

claim: The research was done under a protocol reviewed and approved by the institutional animal care and use committee (IACUC) of University of California San Francisco (UCSF).
source: This research was done under a protocol reviewed and approved by the institutional animal care and use committee (IACUC) of University of California San Francisco (UCSF).
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval for the research.

claim: The fish were kept in a standalone aquatic system (Techniplast, Italy) with water maintained at 28° and a diurnal cycle of 10 hr of dark and 14 hr of light.
source: The fish were kept in a standalone aquatic system (Techniplast, Italy) with water maintained at 28° and a diurnal cycle of 10 hr of dark and 14 hr of light (Aleström et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the husbandry conditions, supported by a citation to Aleström et al., 2020.

claim: The study was conducted on the wild-type EKW strain, casper mutant, and h2afva:h2afva-mCherry transgenic line.
source: The study was conducted on the wild-type EKW strain, casper mutant (White et al., 2008) and h2afva:h2afva-mCherry transgenic line (Knopf et al., 2011) (gift from Jan Huisken, Morgridge Institute for Research, Madison, USA).
evidence: This describes the fish strains used, supported by citations.

claim: Only fish between 4 months and 18 months old were housed and used.
source: We only housed and used fish between 4 months and 18 months old.
evidence: This describes the age range of fish used in the study.

claim: Manual feeding is done once a day, at the same time of the day, according to the manufacturer recommendations and fish density.
source: Manual feeding is done once a day, at the same time of the day, according to the manufacturer recommendations and fish density.
evidence: This describes the manual feeding protocol used as a control.

claim: ZAFs are designed to be built with only commercially-available parts.
source: ZAFs are designed to be built with only commercially-available parts.
evidence: This is supported by the parts lists provided in the supplementary files.

claim: Most of the parts used are generic and can be replaced by similar parts with similar specifications.
source: Most of the parts used are generic and can be replaced by similar parts with similar specifications.
evidence: This is an assertion about the flexibility of the parts selection.

claim: The only component that cannot be easily exchanged is the Raspberry PI computer.
source: The only component that cannot be easily exchanged is the Raspberry PI computer, but this is not an issue as these are very easily sourced.
evidence: This is an assertion about the specificity of components.

claim: The ZAFs frame is built using the versatile and easy to use Makerbeam construction system.
source: To build the ZAFs frame we use the versatile and easy to use Makerbeam consruction system.
evidence: This describes the construction method for the frame.

claim: For both ZAFs, two different tubing sizes are used: 3/8" outside diameter tubes for the pump tubing and 1/4" outside diameter tubes for the valves tubing.
source: For both ZAFs we use two different tubing sizes, for the pump tubing we use 3/8" outside diameter tubes, for the valves tubing we use 1/4" outside diameter tubes.
evidence: This describes the tubing specifications.

claim: Either silicone or PVC based tubing is used because they have good specifications and are safe for food delivery.
source: We use either silicone or PVC based tubing because they have good specifications and are safe for food delivery (PVC based are more cost effective).
evidence: This describes the tubing material choices and their rationale.

claim: The electronic core of ZAF is based on a Raspberry Pi computer, a Servo Hat Board, and Motor Controllers.
source: The electronic core of ZAF is based on (i) A Raspberry a credit card size computer, (ii) A Servo Hat Board to drive Pulse Width Modulation outputs, like the pumps and valve, (iii) Motor Controller to control the DC motors (pumps and valve).
evidence: This describes the electronic components of ZAF.

claim: All the pumps and valves connected to the motor drivers are plugged on a 12V and 10A power supply converter.
source: All the pumps and valves connected to the motor drivers are plugged on a 12V and 10A power supply converter.
evidence: This describes the power supply specifications.

claim: The Raspberry Pi, the servo hat and all the electronics connected to the servo hat are running with 5V through the Raspberry Pi power.
source: The Raspberry Pi, the servo hat and all the electronic connected to the servo hat are running with 5V through the Raspberry Pi power.
evidence: This describes the power specifications for certain components.

claim: ZAF+ electronics are comprised of a Raspberry Pi 3 B+, two Arduino Megas, several motor controllers, and 16 Relay Module interface boards.
source: ZAF+ electronics are comprised of four different components i. A Raspberry Pi 3 B + to run the software and control the electronics, ii. two Arduino Megas Arduino 2,560 microcontrollers for the digital devices, iii. several motor controllers to control the various pumps, iv. 16 Relay Module interface board to drive current and control the valves.
evidence: This describes the electronic components of ZAF+.

claim: The two Arduinos in ZAF+ are daisy-chained via a serial connection.
source: The two Arduinos are daisy-chained via a serial connection (the whole design can be extended by daisy-chaining more arduinos).
evidence: This describes the connection method for the Arduino controllers.

claim: A 12V power supply provides power to the electronics in ZAF+, except for the Raspberry Pi and the two Arduino Megas powered by the Raspberry Pi 5V.
source: A 12V power supply provides power to the electronics, except for the Raspberry Pi and the two Arduino Megas powered by the Raspberry Pi 5V.
evidence: This describes the power supply configuration for ZAF+.

claim: The control software for both ZAFs as well as the corresponding graphical user interfaces are available as open-source code.
source: The control software for both ZAFs as well as the corresponding graphical user interfaces are available as open-source code.
evidence: This describes the availability of the software.

claim: Gemma micro 300 (Skretting Zebrafish) food diet is used for feeding.
source: We use the Gemma micro 300 (Skretting Zebrafish) food diet.
evidence: This describes the food type used in the experiments.

claim: Feeding is calibrated so that ZAF distributes 5% of the fish body weight per feeding.
source: Feeding is calibrated so that ZAF distributes 5% of the fish body weight per feeding.
evidence: This describes the feeding calibration method.

claim: The fish in the facility are fed twice a day.
source: We feed the fish in our facility twice a day.
evidence: This describes the feeding frequency.

claim: ZAF is calibrated to distribute 5 g of food homogeneously to all tanks per run.
source: Based on the number of fish, we calibrate the automatic device to distribute 5 g of food homogeneously to all tanks per run.
evidence: This describes the calibration for ZAF.

claim: Calibration is done manually by adjusting the food container opening and the amount of servo rotation.
source: This calibration is done by manually by adjusting the food container opening, and the amount of servo rotation.
evidence: This describes the calibration method.

claim: ZAF+ runs the feeding program twice a day.
source: Similarly to ZAF, we use the Gemma micro 300 (Skretting Zebrafish) diet and run the program twice a day.
evidence: This describes the feeding frequency for ZAF+.

claim: Food distribution in ZAF+ is done per tank according to a 'food quantity selection' parameter that can be set on the user interface.
source: Food distribution is done per tank according to a 'food quantity selection' parameter that can be set on the user interface: '1' for low fish density, to '4' for high fish densities.
evidence: This describes the food distribution control in ZAF+.

claim: The approximate amount of food required for different fish densities is: Very low - 100 mg for 2–4 fish, low - 200 mg for 5–8 fish, medium - 350 mg for 9–14 fish, large - 500 mg for 15 up to 20 fish.
source: The approximate amount of food required for different fish densities is as follows: Very low - 100 mg for to 2–4 fish, low - 200 mg for 5–8 fish, medium - 350 mg for 9–14 fish, large - 500 mg for 15 up to 20 fish.
evidence: This provides specific calibration values for different fish densities.

claim: To weigh the fish, each fish was dabbed on a tissue paper to remove excess water and then placed in a tared petri dish.
source: To weigh the fish, we first took a clean petri dish and tared it on a weighing scale. Each fish was then dabbed on a tissue paper to remove excess water and then placed in the petri dish to weigh it.
evidence: This describes the method for weighing fish.

claim: The weight of the fish was documented over a period of 7 weeks to demonstrate the feeding efficiency of ZAF+.
source: To demonstrate the feeding efficiency of ZAF+, we documented the weight of the fish over a period of 7 weeks.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for evaluating ZAF+.

claim: The fish were weighed every Monday from week 1 to week 8.
source: The fish were weighed every Monday from week 1 to week 8.
evidence: This describes the weighing schedule.

claim: Two tanks were chosen for evaluation - one with over 12 fish and the second with only four fish.
source: Since ZAF+ has the potential to customize the amount of food given per tank based on the number of fish present, we chose two tanks - one with over 12 fish and the second with only four fish to ensure each tank receives the designated amount of food.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for testing ZAF+ with different fish densities.

claim: These two tanks were kept with the same fish population during the whole evaluation.
source: These two tanks were kept with the same fish population during the whole evaluation.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Tanks from different rows (top and bottom) were used to verify that tube layout and length do not affect the feeding quality nor quantity.
source: We used tanks from different rows (top and bottom) to verify that tube layout and length do not affect the feeding quality nor quantity.
evidence: This describes the experimental design to test for potential confounding factors.

claim: The breeding of the fish was tracked over 2 weeks.
source: Similarly we tracked the breeding of the fish over 2 weeks.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for evaluating breeding.

claim: Three random fish were selected and two to three crosses were bred for each of them.
source: Three random fish were selected and two to three crosses were bred for each of them.
evidence: This describes the breeding experimental design.

claim: The number of crosses which bred for each of the lines was documented and the average of all the positive crosses was calculated.
source: Next day, we documented the number of crosses which bred for each of the lines and calculated the average of all the positive crosses.
evidence: This describes the method for evaluating breeding success.
